events.continuity_hook: Moves the Las Vegas tournament weekend from schedule comparison into booking choices.
events.interaction_goal: Choose the hotel hold, confirm the driving plan, set room and parking details, plan Friday dinner and Saturday early breakfast, note cancellation and payment timing, and prepare a simple Sunday return plan around the championship window.
events.scenario_brief: Tessa is ready to lock in the Las Vegas tournament weekend. The posted schedule makes a Friday afternoon drive from Salt Lake City and a Sunday evening return more practical than airfare for three people, and the hotel hold closest to the sports complex expires tonight. The open questions are whether to accept the closer hotel even though dinner choices are thinner, how to set up a two-queen room for the family, and whether to keep a late-checkout request or plan to load the car before Sunday's games.

events.continuity_hook: Handles the final logistics for the booked Las Vegas tournament weekend.
events.interaction_goal: Set the Friday departure and fuel stops, plan a grab-and-go breakfast for Saturday, map parking for both gyms, decide whether late checkout is still useful, and build a Sunday return plan that works if the last game runs long.
events.scenario_brief: A few days before the Las Vegas drive, the tournament posts court assignments that split Saturday afternoon matches between the main sports complex and an overflow gym about 15 minutes away. The hotel is booked, but breakfast starts too late for the first match, and the weekend forecast shows gusty conditions on parts of I-15. The trip now needs practical timing rather than new reservations.

events.continuity_hook: Begins the first spring yield trip after the fall travel and family weekend are complete.
events.interaction_goal: Compare travel mode, outline the Denver-area driving pattern, shortlist Boulder/Broomfield, Denver Tech Center/Aurora, and airport-area hotels, flag breakfast and dinner logistics, and identify which refundable rooms are worth holding.
events.scenario_brief: After the holiday lull, Tessa starts a late-February Front Range yield loop with a Wednesday counselor breakfast near Boulder, a Wednesday evening admitted-student reception near Denver Tech Center, a Thursday morning transfer fair in Aurora, and a late-Thursday alumni-hosted counselor meetup in Fort Collins. Flying into Denver saves winter driving time but requires a rental car and careful hotel placement; driving from Salt Lake City offers flexibility but adds road-weather uncertainty. The unresolved pieces are fly versus drive, one hotel base versus split nights, and how to keep meals simple around the early and late events.

events.continuity_hook: Refines the Front Range yield loop after event times and venue details change.
events.interaction_goal: Rank the Thursday-night versus Friday-return flight choices, compare one-base and split-night hotel plans, choose the likely overnight areas, note parking and drive-time risks, and pick breakfast and dinner backups near each stop.
events.scenario_brief: The Front Range hosts send updated details before Tessa books: Boulder check-in moves earlier, the Aurora transfer fair shifts to a campus building with limited nearby visitor parking, and the Fort Collins meetup confirms a late-afternoon end time. Denver nonstop flight times still work for an afternoon outbound, but returning Thursday night after Fort Collins would be rushed. Hotel availability is tightening around Boulder because of a campus event, so she needs to decide how many hotel changes are worth avoiding morning stress.

events.continuity_hook: Moves the Front Range yield loop from comparison into reservations.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize flights, rental-car pickup and return times, hotel sequence, room details, window-seat requests, parking costs, breakfast hours, dinner options after the late meetup, cancellation dates, and receipt notes.
events.scenario_brief: The Front Range plan is ready for reservations. The practical setup is Tuesday afternoon Salt Lake City to Denver, a rental car kept through the loop, Tuesday night near Broomfield for the Boulder breakfast, Wednesday night near Aurora or Denver Tech Center, Thursday night by the Denver airport after the Fort Collins meetup, and a Friday early-afternoon return. The remaining decision is whether the extra airport-area hotel change is worth the easier Friday airport buffer.

events.continuity_hook: Handles final timing details for the booked Front Range yield loop.
events.interaction_goal: Set the Tuesday-through-Friday timeline, choose breakfast backups, plan checkout and luggage handling, map the Fort Collins parking approach, schedule dinner after the late event, and protect the Friday fuel, car-return, and bag-drop window.
events.scenario_brief: Eight days before the Front Range trip, the Boulder host asks exhibitors to arrive even earlier, the Fort Collins venue sends a parking map with one nearby lot closed, and the return flight moves slightly earlier. Flights, rental car, and rooms are booked, including the airport-area Thursday night, so the trip needs a final timing pass rather than new searching.
